body:
Field-LWW accepts any client-supplied updated_at. A device with a wildly wrong
clock (or a malicious member) can stamp a field with a far-future timestamp and
every honest edit to that field loses until that moment passes. Reproduced:
push name with updated_at = year 2100 → a later honest rename (server-now
clock) is silently discarded; the field is wedged for all members for 74 years.

The spec (server design §6 "Known caveat") accepts wall-clock LWW skew, but an
unbounded wedge is a much worse failure mode than ordinary skew, and there is a
cheap server-side bound: clamp (or reject with 422) any updated_at more than a
small window ahead of server time (e.g. now + 1h — real skew is minutes, and a
clamp keeps the push flowing while capping the damage; a rejected-row 422 would
instead quarantine an innocent device whose clock is wrong, so clamping is the
friendlier choice). Apply in _parse_clock so it covers items and lists, and
also clamps the merge-relevant created_at.

relates: T-85 (same code area — implement after/with the validation pass).

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/sync.py, server/tests/test_sync_engine.py.
title: Server: clamp client-supplied updated_at — a far-future timestamp wedges a field for everyone
